tools.description:
Resolve the pending approval on a suspended task. Use this when get_task reports status `suspended` — typically a Thorough-mode (mode=plan) task waiting on plan review, or a planner waiting on ask_question answers.

`decision=approve` executes the plan in the same task stream. `decision=decline` sends the plan back for revision using `feedback` (required) — it does NOT cancel the task, and the revised plan needs approval again. To stop a task outright use manage_task action=abort. When the task suspended on a clarifying question, pass the replies in `answers`.

feedback.description: revision guidance; required when declining a plan review

tools.description: File a new security finding. `title` is the only required field, but what you supply decides what Neo will store: a severity of high or critical is rejected without `remediation` (30+ characters), `cwe_ids` and `cvss_score`, and is silently recorded as `info` unless `impact` states a demonstrated effect or `evidence` proves one. Supply the proof with the finding rather than trying to raise its severity afterwards. Use `project_id` to file it into an engagement.

tools.description:
Start a new Neo AI security assessment (pentest, code review, recon, CVE triage, patch validation, and more) or continue an existing one. Pass the objective in `task`, e.g. "Run a security review of https://staging.example.com". Optional parameters mirror POST /api/v1/tasks: title, visibility, project, agent routing, sandbox, secrets, files, memory, and per-run credit/duration/step ceilings.

Pick `mode` deliberately. `agent` (default) dispatches one agent immediately — good for a scoped, well-specified job. `plan` is Thorough mode: a planner gathers information and drafts a reviewable plan, the swarm executes it in parallel, and findings are re-verified before they surface — prefer it for broad or open-ended objectives such as a full-scope pentest. Saying "be thorough" in the prompt does NOT change the mode. `goal` plans once and then runs autonomously to completion. `chat` has limited tools.

In `plan` mode the task suspends for your approval unless you pass auto_execute=true — call approve_task to release or revise the plan. Set ask_question=true to let the planner ask clarifying questions first (also answered via approve_task).

Call list_capabilities to discover valid agent_id, model, and project_id values. Returns a task_id once the task is accepted and queued; Neo then works asynchronously. Next: call get_task to watch progress, then get_issues to read validated findings. Do not poll in a tight loop.

With model auto (the default), Neo also picks a model for each subagent from a curated list your model source can use. Pass subagent_models to replace that list with models you choose, and subagent_reasoning_effort to cap the effort a subagent may use.

task.description: the security objective or prompt for the Neo AI agent

title.description: task title; when set, auto title generation is skipped (max 500 characters)

model.description: LLM model ID, exactly as list_capabilities shows it for your model source. On a Neo account these are Neo model labels; with your own API keys or AI connections they are your provider's exact model IDs. Omit it to let Neo choose for your model source. With auto, Neo also picks a model for each subagent.

mode.description: execution mode: agent (full tools), chat (limited tools), plan (Thorough mode: planner gathers info and drafts a reviewable plan first), or goal (plan once, then autonomously execute and verify)

visibility.description: task visibility: private (default), unlisted, or team

project_id.description: project UUID to scope this task to (see list_capabilities, or create_project). A UUID that is not an existing project creates a new unnamed project — pass an ID you got from list_capabilities or create_project, never an invented one

agent_id.description: route to one specific agent (see list_capabilities); omit to let the AgentSwarm orchestrator pick automatically (default); incompatible with goal mode and with agent_ids

agent_ids.description: restrict AgentSwarm orchestration to these agent IDs; mutually exclusive with agent_id

sandbox_id.description: sandbox UUID to run on (from GET /api/v1/sandboxes); omit to use the Neo-managed cloud sandbox

isolated.description: run in an ephemeral sandbox with no prior user context. Leave this off unless isolation is what the user actually asked for: the default shared sandbox keeps their workspace and prior context, while an ephemeral one starts empty and can be reclaimed while a task sits suspended, which makes a later approve_task unrecoverable. Cannot be combined with browser_session_refs

browser_session_refs.description: warm browser session refs (brs_<hex>) to continue from; cannot be combined with isolated

secrets.description: secret names to expose at runtime (opt-in, from GET /api/v1/secrets); only listed names are resolved

file_keys.description: file references to attach to the task

auto_execute.description: plan mode only: when true the plan runs immediately; when false (the default) the task suspends for review and you must call approve_task to continue. Reject for goal mode, which is always automatic

ask_question.description: allow the planner to ask clarifying questions (default false). When true the task can suspend awaiting answers, which you supply via approve_task

max_iterations.description: execution-verification loop iterations, 0-5 (agent and plan modes only). Defaults to 0 for agent mode and 1 for plan mode; rejected for goal mode

max_steps.description: max LLM steps for the execution phase, 4-200 (agent and plan modes only). Rejected for goal mode. Note: usage-plan limits override this on metered plans

max_duration_seconds.description: cumulative active runtime ceiling in seconds, 300-86400 (defaults to 86400); approval suspension time is excluded

memory_off.description: do not read or update memory from previous tasks; current-task working memory still applies

completion_delivery.description: completion handoff: webhook (POST to the team webhook) or artifact (persist for GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}/artifacts). Omit for no handoff

source.description: inbox source: hackerone, github, or gmail

external_id.description: HackerOne report id, GHSA id, or Gmail thread id

context.description: program handle (HackerOne), owner/repo (GitHub), or mailbox email (Gmail)

triage_ref.description: link this task to a HackerOne, GitHub, or Gmail inbox item; forces team visibility

task_id.description: existing task UUID to continue a conversation

subagent_models.description: models Neo may use for subagents, as exact model IDs (see list_capabilities), in order of preference; replaces the default list. Omit to let auto pick from a curated list your model source can use

subagent_reasoning_effort.description: the highest reasoning effort a subagent may use: auto (no ceiling, the default), low, medium, high, or max

tools.description:
Change a finding's classification or add a comment. `action` is one of:
- `update` (requires `issue_id`) — set any of severity, status, confidence, priority, assignee, tags/tags_add/tags_remove.
- `bulk_update` (requires `issue_ids`, max 1000) — apply the same change to several findings at once.
- `comment` (requires `issue_id` and `comment`) — record a note without changing any field.
- `delete` (requires `issue_id` and `confirm`) — remove one finding permanently.
- `bulk_delete` (requires `issue_ids` and `confirm`) — remove several permanently.

`update` also edits the finding's body: title, description, impact, remediation, reproduction_steps, evidence, cvss_score, cwe_ids, cve_ids, references, target details, ticket links, and due_date. Deleting is irreversible and loses the finding's history — prefer status `false_positive` or `duplicate`, which keep the record.

Moving a finding to `false_positive` or `accepted_risk` retires it from the active set and requires `comment` explaining why; the reason is stored on every affected finding and shows up in get_issue view=timeline. Call get_issue first — re-classifying a finding whose evidence you have not read is how real vulnerabilities get closed by mistake.

Neo will not store a severity above `info` for a finding with no demonstrated impact: it rewrites the severity, and drags status and confidence down with it, while still reporting success. `action=update` compares what it sent against what came back and tells you when that happened — read that notice rather than assuming the value you asked for was stored.

action.description: what to do: update, bulk_update, or comment

issue_id.description: UUID of the finding (required when action=update or action=comment)

issue_ids.description: UUIDs of the findings to change (required when action=bulk_update, max 1000)

false_positive_reason.description: structured reason stored on the finding when status=false_positive; defaults to comment

risk_acceptance_reason.description: structured reason stored on the finding when status=accepted_risk; defaults to comment

description.description: what the finding is and how it was reached

impact.description: what an attacker gains; state the demonstrated effect, not the theoretical one — this is part of what lets Neo store a severity above info

remediation.description: how to fix it; required and at least 30 characters for high or critical severity

reproduction_steps.description: ordered steps that reproduce the finding

tools.description:
Start a Neo task against a pull request and return its task_id, which get_task then follows. `command` selects what it does:
- `review` — security review of the diff (the default choice)
- `full_review` — review the whole changed surface, not just the diff
- `investigate` — dig into a specific question; pass it in `message`
- `summary` — plain-language summary of the change
- `fix` — **writes to GitHub**: pushes remediation commits to the PR's branch
- `create_issue` — **writes to GitHub**: opens an issue on the repository
- `freeform` — run `message` as the instruction

`fix` and `create_issue` change the repository and need `confirm` set to true. The others only produce a review. Runs are asynchronous and consume credits, so check get_pull_request for an existing review before starting another.

pull_number.description: the pull request number as GitHub shows it

command.description: what to run: review (default), full_review, investigate, summary, fix, create_issue, or freeform

message.description: extra instructions; required for investigate and freeform

confirm.description: must be true for fix and create_issue, which write to GitHub

tools.description: Browse or search the Explore directory of shareable Neo agents: public agents plus any team agents shared with you. Use it to find an agent you have not installed yet; use list_capabilities for the agents already on your account. Each result carries two identifiers — `uuid` (pass to get_agent / install_agent) and `agent_id` (pass to create_task once installed). Unlisted agents are deliberately not searchable; open them by UUID or Explore link with get_agent. Read-only.

query.description: search text matched against agent name and description

tags.description: comma-separated tags; matches agents carrying any of them

visibility.description: restrict to public or team agents; omit for both

offset.description: number of agents to skip, for paging

tools.name: search_agents
tools.title: Search the agent directory

tools.description: Send mid-run input to a task that is already working, without stopping it. The text is injected at the agent's next step, so use it to redirect scope, answer a question the run raised, or add a constraint — `abort` stops a run, this one changes its course. Only useful while a task is running; a finished task has no next step to inject into.

text.description: the instruction to inject at the agent's next step

stream_id.description: live stream UUID this input was typed against; the call fails if that stream is no longer live

tools.name: send_task_input
tools.title: Steer a running task

tools.description: Write a UTF-8 text file into your workspace and return its file_key, which create_task and create_schedule accept in `file_keys`. Use it to attach scope documents, target lists, rules of engagement, or configuration an assessment needs to read. `file_key` must start with workspace/. Text only — this tool cannot carry binary content; upload those through the web UI. An existing file at the same key is overwritten.

file_key.description: destination path starting with workspace/ (e.g. workspace/scope/targets.txt)
